clue.text: Approach for sudden attack

definitions.meaning: a way in or means of reaching something

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are dictionary meanings: a route of entry, and an old word for a sudden fit of illness or emotion.

clue.text: Meant perhaps to retain: some rooms

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold another piece inside them
perhaps flags that Meant is only one arrangement of its letters

parts.note: part means some, a portion

explanation.surface: Someone intends to keep a few rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges Meant to AMENT; 'Meant' looks like the verb of the sentence but is only fodder, and 'to retain' wraps the shuffle round the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is a set of rooms forming one dwelling.

clue.text: A thick rope with a soft inside is 'quite adequate

indicators.note: the a-and-soft letters go inside the rope word

parts.note: a cable is a heavy rope, as for mooring
P stands for piano, soft in music

explanation.surface: A heavy rope with a soft core does the job well enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A competent person or thing is fully up to the task.

clue.text: Artisan — a man well-qualified to, intervene in, weighty issue

indicators.note: to come between, so the qualified man sits between the other two pieces

parts.note: a stone is a unit of weight, fourteen pounds
a son is a child, one's issue
MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A skilled worker is just the man to step into a serious dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of body weight, fourteen pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who cuts and dresses building stone is a skilled artisan.

clue.text: A summary of Jack's 29 ac

parts.note: Jack is a sailor, as is AB (able seaman); several of them make ABS
the answer to 29 across is a long written essay, which is also a tract

explanation.surface: A request for a précis of some sailor's long essay.
explanation.walkthrough: '29 ac' points to the answer of 29 across, a formal paper, whose synonym supplies the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstract is a short précis placed at the head of a paper.

clue.text: See the responsibility of the office

definitions.meaning: the diocese over which a bishop rules
the office or rank of a bishop

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a diocese, a bishop's see, and the post a bishop holds.

clue.text: High water

parts.note: reads like high tide, but means water lying high up in the hills

explanation.definitionFit: A small mountain lake lies at height.

clue.text: Lady's maid in trouble under a large cap.

indicators.note: in a down answer the trouble word sits below the others

parts.note: big means large
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A maid in difficulties beneath a big hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cap.' says that A BIG caps the down answer, sitting above AIL; 'in' is a link. An abigail is an old term for a lady's maid, from a character in Beaumont and Fletcher.
explanation.definitionFit: The name became a general term for a waiting-woman after a servant character in a seventeenth-century play.

clue.text: Article on feet that's really taking

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An article about feet that is truly captivating.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is taking something for real, not just being attractive.

clue.text: Hold a strong position

definitions.meaning: the central tower of a castle, its stronghold

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to retain something and the fortified tower of a castle.

clue.text: Commend parking in a test

indicators.note: the parking letter is set inside the phrase a test

parts.note: to prove something is to test it, as in proving ground
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Praise for getting a parking space during a driving test.
explanation.definitionFit: To commend something is to speak favourably of it, to sanction it.

clue.text: Menial has to dish up about one litre

indicators.note: the dish-up word goes around the one-and-litre letters

parts.note: to dish up food is to serve it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lowly kitchen worker must ladle out roughly a litre of soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A menial attitude is slavish and fawning, like a servant's.

clue.text: Spinning a bent spool — it serves

indicators.note: spinning round throws the letters of a bent spool into a new order

explanation.surface: A bent spool spinning on a machine, which somehow keeps working.
explanation.definitionFit: A large spoon used for serving food at table is the item meant.

clue.text: The affected piety of 26 dn

definitions.meaning: the answer to 26 down, meaning a lean or tilt

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both sanctimonious humbug and a slope or tilt, as a ship may heel over.

clue.text: The beauty may be no less evil "

indicators.note: may be suggests a possible rearrangement of the letters of no less evil

explanation.surface: Beauty might be no less wicked than anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Loveliness is a synonym for beauty.

clue.text: Anti-irritant extracted from the yew, ash, and willow

indicators.note: the letters are pulled out of the run of words that follows, spanning three of them

explanation.surface: A soothing lotion made from the bark of three common trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion for bathing sore eyes counteracts irritation there.

clue.text: Capital cover arranged by a man with adroitness

parts.note: he refers to a man
address in an old sense means skill or dexterity

explanation.surface: A man skilfully arranges a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' here means of the head, not a city; 'arranged by' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is the body's top, its capital, and this ornamental item covers it.

clue.text: Acted like a swine to other ranks, rebuffed but went ahead

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so the words to and other ranks are read backwards together

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks
led means went in front

explanation.surface: A boorish officer was piggish to the soldiers, was snubbed, and carried on regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigs dig about with their snouts in search of food, a habit described by this verb.

clue.text: Depression about French soil check

indicators.note: the dent goes around the French word

parts.note: a dent is a hollow, a depression
terre is French for earth or soil

explanation.surface: A hollow in French ground stops progress.
explanation.definitionFit: A deterrent is something that checks or restrains action.

clue.text: Medical man invested in instrument — a chancy business

indicators.note: the doctor is clothed inside the instrument, as if put into it

parts.note: a tool is an instrument or implement
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor puts money into a medical device, a risky venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrument' tempts as a musical one; it is a plain tool. A tombola is a British raffle drawn from a revolving drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A raffle-style lottery depends entirely on luck, a game of chance.

clue.text: The authority to give a fellow time

parts.note: a man is a fellow
a date is a fixed time

explanation.surface: Permission is needed to give a man a time slot.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official authorisation or commission.

clue.text: Old device for pitch illumination

parts.note: reads like floodlights for a sports pitch, but means an iron basket holding burning tar as a beacon

explanation.definitionFit: This historic iron vessel held burning pitch or oil to give light as a torch or beacon.

clue.text: Having rested, one dined content

parts.note: sat means having rested in a seat
I is the Roman numeral for one
ate means dined

explanation.surface: After resting, one has eaten and is happy.
explanation.definitionFit: To content an appetite is to satisfy it fully.

clue.text: Notes the price is very cheap

definitions.meaning: a tune is a sequence of musical notes
from the idiom going for a ___, bought very cheaply

explanation.definitionFit: A tune is a series of notes, and the idiom 'for a song' means at a bargain price.

clue.text: Suffer to appear chic?

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to sting with pain and to be stylish.

clue.text: Stared curiously, around little, run

indicators.note: the shuffled letters wrap around the little word
curiously means in an odd way, so the letters of Stared are rearranged

parts.note: mini means little, as in a miniskirt

explanation.surface: Someone stared oddly around the room at a little runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' makes ADSTER from the six letters, and 'around' wraps that round the small word; 'run' is the definition in its sense of managing, not sprinting.
explanation.definitionFit: To run an organisation or estate is to manage it.

clue.text: Rations, perhaps, for the club

definitions.meaning: a golf club with a metal head

explanation.definitionFit: The metal names both emergency rations and a golf club.

clue.text: Landed about a quarter-a record

indicators.note: the landed word goes around the quarter letter

parts.note: lit means landed or alighted, as a bird lit on a branch
S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Arrived at around a quarter past, a record time.
explanation.definitionFit: A list is a record of items written down.

clue.text: "So for a good old-gentlemanly vice, I think I must take up with " (Byron)

definitions.text: "So for a good old-gentlemanly vice, I think I must take up with " (Byron)

parts.words: "So for a good old-gentlemanly vice, I think I must take up with " (Byron)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Byron's Don Juan, where the missing word is a vice of old men

explanation.definitionFit: Byron's Don Juan names greed for money as the fitting vice of an elderly gentleman.

clue.text: Ring through at one point for work

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
per means through or by means of, as in per post
E, east, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A phone call put through at some stage about a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To run or function, as a machine does, is to work.

clue.text: A tree — it's used to make paper

indicators.note: the words are raw material from which the answer is made, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: its, taken without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A tree is the source of the pulp from which paper is made.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholarly paper is a formal written discourse on a subject.

clue.text: Like a little money? A rise is what's needed!

parts.note: as means like, as in as good as gold
a cent is a coin of small value

explanation.surface: Someone short of cash asks for a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb or upward slope is a rise.
